raw_response:
I'm 49, been farming these 30 years on my 7.5 mu here in Quzhou. Just me and my wife now — two of us — so every decision has to think about labor and cash. We keep 5 mu in the wheat-maize double crop, that's our bread and butter, and 2.5 mu in cotton for extra income and to spread the risk. If one crop fails, we still have the other.

**Wheat:** I'll plant in early October, same as everyone in the village. I buy improved seed, about 25 yuan per mu. The extension guy says 15 kg of nitrogen per mu is enough, but I've learned on my own land that 16 kg works better — I put half down as base fertilizer before planting, and the other half at jointing in March when the wheat greens up. I also add some phosphate and potash, about 7 kg and 3 kg per mu. I'll irrigate twice: once in winter if the soil's too dry, and once at jointing. Pumping water costs money, about 30 yuan each time per mu, so I don't overdo it. Last year I got 420 kg per mu; this year I'm hoping for 430 if spring is good.

**Maize:** This is the tricky one. After wheat harvest in early June, we have maybe a week to get maize in the ground. I plant hybrid seed, about 42 yuan per mu. No time for much tillage — just minimal cultivation and plant right away. I put all fertilizer down at planting: about 15 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, 3 kg potassium per mu. For irrigation, maybe once in July if it's dry at flowering. Maize is shorter season and handles drought better than wheat, so I don't push it. Expecting around 480 kg per mu.

**Cotton:** The 2.5 mu gets planted in late April. Cotton seed costs about 32 yuan per mu. I use less fertilizer than wheat — about 12 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, 3 kg potassium per mu — split between planting and flowering. Cotton needs more pesticide, especially for bollworm, so I budget for herbicide and insecticide. I'll irrigate twice, once at flowering and once at boll formation. The hard part is picking — many passes, and with just two of us we can't manage more than 2.5 mu. Hoping for 260 kg of lint per mu.

**Costs and tradeoffs:** Seeds, fertilizer, pesticide, and irrigation will run me about 2,800 yuan this year. That's a big chunk of what I've saved. I always keep some cash back for emergencies — never spend everything on inputs. I thought about hiring labor during wheat harvest and maize planting, but at 120 yuan per day I can't afford it. Me and my wife will manage. It's tight that week between crops, but we've done it for 30 years.
